One team: film it, post it, run it.

posts.caption_en:
The video is beautiful. Nobody finishes it.

Most brand videos open with a logo. Those first three seconds decide the fate of everything you paid for.

How we cut instead:
· A visual event inside the first 1.5 seconds
· Burned-in subtitles, Myanmar and English — sound-off is the default
· The logo lands at the end, not the start

Beautiful is the entry fee. Holding someone to the last frame is the work.
posts.cta: Send us your last video — we'll tell you where it loses people.

· တစ် post မှာ တောင်းဆိုချက် တစ်ခုတည်း ရှိလား

posts.caption_en:
How many posts a month does it take to sell?

Wrong question. Some businesses sell on eight. Some post thirty and move nothing.

Three things decide it:
· The first line — written for one person, or for everyone?
· The Myanmar — does it read like a person wrote it, or a translator?
· One ask per post — or two, so both get ignored?

Get those right and eight is enough. Get them wrong and thirty is just a faster way to spend.
posts.cta: Post your worst-performing first line — we'll rewrite it.

posts.caption_mm:

ရန်ကုန်မှာ အများဆုံး ဖြစ်တတ်တာတွေ —
· ည ၂ နာရီ ဖြုတ်သိမ်းချိန် — crew နှုန်း ၁.၅ ဆကနေ ၂ ဆ တက်သွားတယ်
· LED အရွယ်အစား နောက်ဆုံးမှ ပြောင်း — ကြိုတင်မှာထားတာ အလကား
· မိုးရွာရင် ဘာလုပ်မလဲ မရှိတာ — ဒါက အစီအစဉ် မဟုတ်ပါဘူး

ဒါကြောင့် ကျွန်တော်တို့ budget တိုင်းမှာ ၁၀% အရန်ငွေကို စာရင်းတစ်ကြောင်း အနေနဲ့ ထည့်ထားပါတယ် — ဖျောက်မထားပါဘူး။ ငွေလဲနှုန်းကိုလည်း ဈေးကွက်နှုန်းနဲ့ တွက်ပြီး သုံးထားတဲ့ရက်စွဲကို ရေးထားပါတယ်။

ပွဲအပြီး ၇ ရက်အတွင်း အစီရင်ခံစာ ပေးပါတယ်။
posts.caption_en:
A cost that appears after the event isn't a cost. It's a wound.

The three that catch Yangon events most often:
· A 2am strike — crew rates jump 1.5–2×
· LED size changed late — the booking you paid for is wasted
· No wet-weather plan — which means there is no plan

So every budget we issue carries a 10% contingency as a visible line, never quietly absorbed. Every figure converts at market FX with the rate and date written on it.

Post-event report within 7 days. Always.
posts.cta: Planning something? Send the date first — availability decides everything.

content.month_theme: What we do, priced in the open.

design_system.art_direction: Editorial, not promotional. Every asset should look like a page torn from a well-set business document rather than a social graphic — deep navy fields, generous margins, one gold accent doing one job per frame. The work is confident enough to be quiet: no gradients, no glow, no stock imagery of people pointing at laptops. Where photography appears it is real work, real rooms, real Yangon light. The system's job is to make a small agency look like the most rigorous one in the room, at thumbnail size, on a mid-range Android in daylight.

palette.name: ZYNTH Navy
palette.use: Primary field for 70% of assets. Backgrounds and full-bleed panels. Never as body text on gold.

palette.name: ZYNTH Gold
palette.use: Accent only — one element per frame: a rule, a number, a CTA chip, or a highlighted word. Never a background, never two gold elements competing in one frame.

palette.name: Off-White
palette.use: Primary text on navy; also the alternate light field for teaching/carousel frames where reading length is high.

palette.name: Charcoal
palette.use: Body text on off-white fields, and secondary UI marks. Not for headlines — headlines are navy or off-white.

palette.name: Slate
palette.use: Captions, metadata, dates, source lines, disclaimers such as 'indicative — RFQ'. Never for anything that must be read at thumbnail size.

typography.headline: A confident geometric sans (Inter Tight / Söhne class), 600–700 weight. Feed headline 44–72pt at 1080px canvas. Sentence case, never all-caps except the IGNITE wordmark. Maximum 9 words — if it needs 10, the copy is wrong, not the layout.
typography.body: Same family, 400 weight, 24–30pt at 1080px, line-height 1.45, measure capped at 34 characters on square formats. Left-aligned always; centred body text is banned in this system.
typography.myanmar: Pyidaungsu (or Noto Sans Myanmar) — never a Latin face with Myanmar glyphs faked in. Line-height 1.9 minimum to clear stacked diacritics, and 15% larger optical size than the Latin equivalent to match perceived weight. Myanmar and English never share a line; they stack, with a 24px gold rule between them. Never letter-space Myanmar text.
typography.hierarchy_rules: One idea per frame, three levels maximum: headline, one supporting line, one CTA chip. Numbers are typographic events — when a frame has a number worth reading (12, 16, 35%, 50 days), it is set 2–3× the headline size and everything else recedes.

templates.name: Statement
templates.use_for: static_post, testimonial — one idea, maximum impact
templates.layout: Full-bleed navy. Headline set in the upper two-thirds, left-aligned, 96px margins. Gold rule (4px, 120px wide) sits above the headline as an entry mark. Logo bottom-left at 48px, CTA chip bottom-right. Bottom 220px kept clear of critical elements for feed UI overlap.
templates.dimensions: 1080×1350 (4:5) for feed; 1080×1080 square variant for LinkedIn

templates.name: Teach
templates.use_for: carousel, educational — sequential reasoning that must be read
templates.layout: Off-white field, charcoal body, navy headline. 12-column grid, content in columns 2–11. Frame number top-right in slate. Gold rule under the frame headline. Final frame flips to navy for the takeaway plus CTA — the colour flip IS the ending.

templates.name: Ledger
templates.use_for: pricing, budget, FX and any frame carrying figures
templates.layout: Off-white field with a fine slate rule between every line item, figures right-aligned in a fixed 320px column, one gold total row. Reads as a document, not a graphic. No icons anywhere in this template.

templates.name: Summit
templates.layout: Near-black navy (#0D1729 tint of the primary) with the IGNITE wordmark locked top-left and the date as the dominant typographic element. Optional duotone photography at 35% opacity behind, navy/gold duotone only. Tier or outcome lists set in two columns with gold ticks.

templates.name: Proof
templates.layout: Split field — 40% navy metric block left, 60% off-white context right (stacked vertically on portrait). The metric is the largest element on the canvas. Any unverified or withheld figure carries a slate 'indicative' or 'withheld by client' mark; figures are never invented to fill the block.

layout_rules: One gold element per frame. If a second wants to exist, the first one wasn't doing its job.
Headline maximum 9 words, and it must be legible when the asset is 120px wide — check every frame at that size before it ships.
Bottom 220px of any 4:5 asset stays clear of critical content (feed UI, caption fold).
Myanmar text never shares a line with English; it stacks below, separated by a 24px gold rule, at 1.9 line-height.
No icons in Ledger or Statement templates. Icons are permitted only in Teach, at 32px, single-weight, and never more than three per frame.
No drop shadows, no gradients, no glass effects, no glow. Depth comes from the field change, not from an effect.
Photography is real or it is absent. Generated imagery may only ever be an abstract background or texture — never a person, product, premises or result presented as real.
design_system.photography_direction: Documentary, available light, slightly underexposed to keep navy shadows rich. Real desks, real Yangon rooms, real crew at work — the camera is an observer, never a director. Hands and screens over faces where a face isn't necessary. Colour graded cool in the shadows so it sits with the navy field; skin tones stay natural, never teal. No smiling stock, no handshakes, no laptops on cafe tables with nothing on the screen.
graphic_devices: The gold entry rule — 4px × 120px, sits above every headline, the system's signature mark
The number as hero — figures set 2–3× headline size, the only permitted 'loud' element
The strike-through in gold — used exclusively to show what was cut or corrected (P05, P07)
The interval bracket — two rules with a gap, used to show a gap between two values (P13 FX)
The colour flip — carousel takeaway frames invert from off-white to navy, marking the ending
design_system.accessibility: Off-white #F5F3EF on navy #12203A = 13.1:1, and charcoal #2B2B2B on off-white = 13.6:1 — both far clear of WCAG AA. Gold #B88A2A on navy is 4.9:1: acceptable for headlines and large numbers, never for body text or anything below 24pt. Minimum on-asset text size 24pt at 1080px canvas. Every video carries burned-in subtitles in both languages (sound-off is the default), minimum 32pt with a 60%-opacity navy scrim behind. Every published asset also needs alt text — written by whoever schedules it, in the caption's primary language.
asset_checklist: ZYNTH logo in SVG plus a light-background variant — the current PNG is being scaled and it shows
Licensed weights of the headline family for both web and print, or a confirmed open-source substitute
Pyidaungsu / Noto Sans Myanmar installed on every machine that touches an asset
A real photography set from the office and one client shoot — 20+ usable frames so the system stops depending on type alone
The IGNITE wordmark lockup with clear-space rules, and venue photography cleared for commercial use
Written permission for any client name, quote or figure published in P05, P09 and P12
open_questions: Headline typeface is specified by class, not by licence — confirm which family ZYNTH owns before week 1 production.
Is there an approved dark-mode variant of the logo? Assets currently assume gold-on-navy throughout.
Video subtitle style should be locked once and reused; currently specified per post, which will drift.
